key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings form denser, fine-lamellar microstructures with better long-term corrosion and wear performance when droplet spread is high and porosity is low.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters and humidity exposure can improve the durability of Fe-based protective coatings on carbon steel in corrosive and tribological service.
method: Detonation spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under different spraying parameters.
Compare coating microstructure, porosity, corrosion resistance, and wear behavior across humidity environments.
Evaluate tribo-chemical effects during sliding against Si3N4 balls in the presence of water molecules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and tribology testing and shows that higher porosity lowers long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces both friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: The performance gains depend strongly on spray quality and environmental humidity, so coating reliability may drop if porosity defects or service conditions are not well controlled.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
